page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is an x86_64 cloud server instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, designed for workloads requiring a substantial memory footprint and high-capacity local storage. The system features 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading. It provides 192 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Storage is directly integrated, provisioning 5760 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without dedicated GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity and exceptional uncached memory throughput. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves top-quartile results with a single-core score of 2,922.47 and a multi-core score of 69,366.22. Memory subsystem testing shows top-decile large-block uncached read and write bandwidths of 467.73 GB/sec and 282.99 GB/sec, respectively. General processing metrics place in the middle tier, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,840.0, a PassMark CPU score of 38,720.99, and Redis performance reaching 51.19 million SET operations per second.

The combination of dedicated CPU allocations, high memory density, and 5.76 TB of bundled NVMe storage provides strong cost efficiency for data-heavy architectures that would otherwise require separate detached block storage volumes. While raw clock frequency is moderate at 2.0 GHz, the sustained multi-core performance and large memory bandwidth make this instance suitable for large relational database engines, memory-intensive key-value stores, real-time analytics, and data pipeline processing.

Benchmark evaluations place its multi-core stress-ng score in the top 25% and its large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths in the top 10%, registering 467.73 GB/sec and 282.99 GB/sec. Mid-tier ratings across PassMark and Geekbench reflect balanced general execution alongside strong continuous throughput. With an 8 GB per vCPU memory ratio and high bundled storage capacity, this instance offers efficient resource concentration for memory-intensive caching layers, high-volume transactional databases, and real-time data analytics pipelines.
